# NVM Command Set 1.3: Complete Independent Course and Engineering Reference

Purpose: a source-located engineering report for GitHub Pages and a 100-minute presentation.

Scope: NVM Command Set 1.3 Chapters 1–5 and Appendix A, with required Base figure dependencies. Sections retain local/PCIe and transport-independent semantics, including the memory-based template in §5.4. Only PCIe/memory-based and common NVMe content appears below.

## Source versions

NVM Express NVM Command Set Specification, Revision 1.3
NVM Express Base Specification, Revision 2.4

Verification date: 2026-09-03. No additional errata, ECNs, Technical Proposals, controller-vendor documents, or source text from the external PCI Express Base Specification are included.

## Reading map

```text
Namespace and format -> Command and limits -> Protection and placement -> Completion and evidence
```

Identify the namespace and format before constructing commands; apply supported integrity, placement, and management rules, then verify through CQEs, Identify, logs, and events.

## Normative language

shall is mandatory, may permits a choice, should expresses a preferred recommendation, and optional means support is not required. The report preserves these terms and never promotes one into another.

## Acronyms first: complete glossary

Every abbreviation below is introduced before it is used in the slide narrative. The term alone is never enough: retain owner, width, unit, scope, and state.

| Acronym / term | Plain-language meaning | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `LBA` | Logical Block Address, measured in blocks of the selected format. | NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §1.1-1.6; 4.1.3.9; 4.1.4.8; 4.1.5, printed pp. 9-12,73-75,79-83, PDF pp. 9-12,73-75,79-83 |
| `NSZE` | Namespace Size, the total number of addressable logical blocks. | NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.1.1; 4.1.5.1, printed pp. 13-14,85-93, PDF pp. 13-14,85-93 |
| `NCAP` | Namespace Capacity, the maximum number of simultaneously allocated logical blocks. | NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.1.1; 4.1.5.1, printed pp. 13-14,85-93, PDF pp. 13-14,85-93 |
| `NUSE` | Namespace Utilization, the number of currently allocated logical blocks. | NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.1.1; 4.1.5.1, printed pp. 13-14,85-93, PDF pp. 13-14,85-93 |
| `AWUN` | Atomic Write Unit Normal, the controller’s zero-based normal atomic-write size. | NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.1.4; 4.1.3.4; 5.9, printed pp. 15-21,66-67,165, PDF pp. 15-21,66-67,165 |
| `AWUPF` | Atomic Write Unit Power Fail, the zero-based atomic size for failure conditions. | NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.1.4; 4.1.3.4; 5.9, printed pp. 15-21,66-67,165, PDF pp. 15-21,66-67,165 |
| `NLB` | Number of Logical Blocks; this field in the report’s commands/status descriptors is zero-based. DSM LLB is separately one-based. | NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §3.3.4; 3.3.6, printed pp. 48-51,53-56, PDF pp. 48-51,53-56 |
| `PRACT` | Protection Information Action; PI handling depends on command and MS. | NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.1.5; 5.3.2-5.3.3, printed pp. 21-22,141-152, PDF pp. 21-22,141-152 |
| `PRCHK` | Protection Information Check bits for Guard, Application, and Reference. | NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.1.5; 5.3.2-5.3.3, printed pp. 21-22,141-152, PDF pp. 21-22,141-152 |
| `STC` | Storage Tag Check, separate from three-bit PRCHK and ignored when STS=0. | NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.1.5; 5.3.2-5.3.3, printed pp. 21-22,141-152, PDF pp. 21-22,141-152 |
| `STS` | Storage Tag Size, the high-bit count within fixed Storage/Reference Space. | NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §5.3.1; 4.1.5.3, printed pp. 97-102,130-138, PDF pp. 97-102,130-138 |
| `LBADS` | LBA Data Size exponent; data bytes=2^LBADS, while zero means currently unavailable. | NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §4.1.5.1; 4.1.5.3; 5.6, printed pp. 85-94,96-102,160-162, PDF pp. 85-94,96-102,160-162 |
| `NLBAF` | Zero-based count of LBA formats with common attributes. | NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §4.1.5.1; 4.1.5.3; 5.6, printed pp. 85-94,96-102,160-162, PDF pp. 85-94,96-102,160-162 |
| `NULBAF` | Actual count of Unique Attribute LBA Formats; zero is allowed. | NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §4.1.5.1; 4.1.5.3; 5.6, printed pp. 85-94,96-102,160-162, PDF pp. 85-94,96-102,160-162 |
| `LBAFEE` | Host LBA Format Extension Enable declaration. | NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §4.1.2; 4.1.3.7, printed pp. 62-63,68-69, PDF pp. 62-63,68-69 |
| `DULBE` | Deallocated or Unwritten Logical Block Error Enable, requiring namespace DAE support. | NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §3.3.3.2.1; 4.1.3.3, printed pp. 47-48,66, PDF pp. 47-48,66 |

## Visual atlas: locate the system before reading fields

Each redraw answers a different question: architecture locates components, sequence shows ownership, decode turns bits into engineering values, and state views preserve failure evidence. These are teaching redraws, not copies of specification artwork.

### Visual 01: Reading map and units

**View type:** `architecture`

```text
1. Namespace
2. Format
3. Command
4. Completion
5. Evidence
```

**Question answered:** This course follows namespaces and formats through command completion, integrity, and management evidence. Use four sessions of roughly 25 minutes for the main path, with figure worksheets and questions for further study. Chapter 1 terminology and reference conventions are included.

**Supporting Figures:** Figure 1, Figure 2

**Sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §1.1-1.6; 4.1.3.9; 4.1.4.8; 4.1.5, printed pp. 9-12,73-75,79-83, PDF pp. 9-12,73-75,79-83

### Visual 02: Namespace capacity and allocation

**View type:** `architecture`

```text
1. NSID
2. NSZE
3. NCAP
4. NUSE
5. Allocation
```

**Question answered:** Separate logical address space from allocated resources before considering writes and deallocation. Returned data and allocation state answer different questions.

**Supporting Figures:** Figure 123

**Sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.1.1; 4.1.5.1, printed pp. 13-14,85-93, PDF pp. 13-14,85-93

### Visual 03: Ordering and Compare-and-Write

**View type:** `architecture`

```text
1. Host dependency
2. Compare
3. Match gate
4. Write
5. Two CQEs
```

**Question answered:** First establish the ordering requirement, then decide whether conditional updating is needed. A fused operation protects comparison and update of the same LBA range, with atomic-size limits checked separately.

**Supporting Figures:** Figure 3

**Sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.1.2-2.1.3, printed pp. 14-15, PDF pp. 14-15

### Visual 04: Normal, power-fail, and multiple atomicity

**View type:** `architecture`

```text
1. NSABP
2. Decode size
3. Check boundaries
4. MAM or single
5. Failure outcome
```

**Question answered:** Read size, starting alignment, NSABP, and MAM together. Atomicity and persistence on nonvolatile media are separate checks; FUA/Flush do not establish ordering for other commands.

**Supporting Figures:** Figure 4, Figure 5, Figure 6, Figure 7, Figure 8, Figure 9, Figure 10

**Sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.1.4; 4.1.3.4; 5.9, printed pp. 15-21,66-67,165, PDF pp. 15-21,66-67,165

```text
1. Controller type
2. Capability
3. Opcode and NSID
4. SCT plus SC
5. Recovery
```

**Question answered:** Build a command/Feature/log capability matrix starting from controller type. A data pointer may reference user data or merely control descriptors.

**Supporting Figures:** Figure 13, Figure 14, Figure 15, Figure 16, Figure 17, Figure 18, Figure 19, Figure 20, Figure 22

**Sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.2; 3.1; 3.3, printed pp. 22-27, PDF pp. 22-27

**View type:** `architecture`

```text

2. Compare or Verify
```

**Question answered:** Expected-content comparison, integrity verification, and ordinary Read provide different evidence. Compare excludes PI from metadata comparison and checks PI separately as requested.

```text
2. Destination range

```

**Question answered:** Calculate the expanded destination range before checking formats, limits, overlap, and atomicity. Copy reduces host data movement but is not an unconditional transaction.

```text
2. Destination PI
```

**Question answered:** Classify whether source and destination use PI, then choose PRINFOR.PRACT and PRINFOW.PRACT. Every source must fit the selected mode.

**Sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §3.3.2.3-3.3.2.4; 5.3.2.5, printed pp. 40-43,146-150, PDF pp. 40-43,146-150

```text
5. Allocation evidence
```

**Question answered:** Determine whether each block satisfies all three limits before applying NVMDSMSV. Separate range/hint validity, attribute processing obligations, and actual media actions.

**View type:** `architecture`

```text
1. DAE
2. DULBE
3. DRB
```

**Question answered:** First determine whether successful reading is permitted, then interpret returned bytes. Allocation status, DRB, and PI have separate conditions.

**Supporting Figures:**

**View type:** `architecture`

```text

2. Range or NSZ
```

**Question answered:** Neither command transfers a host user-data payload, but both change namespace semantics. Identify range mode before checking PI and size limits.

**View type:** `architecture`

**Question answered:** Write down the roles of CNS, CSI, NSID, and Format Index for each query. Zero-filled results have different meanings across queries and do not always mean absent or unsupported.

### Visual 29: Packing Storage/Reference Tags into Dwords

**View type:** `architecture`

```text
1. PI space width
2. STS
3. Storage and reference
4. CDW2 and CDW3
5. CDW14
```

**Question answered:** Determine total space width, split the tags, then pack command Dwords. Similar names do not make Write values interchangeable with Read expected values.

**Supporting Figures:** Figure 166, Figure 167, Figure 168, Figure 169, Figure 170, Figure 171, Figure 172, Figure 173

**Sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §5.3.1.4, printed pp. 137-141, PDF pp. 137-141

### Visual 30: Combining PRACT with PRCHK/STC

**View type:** `architecture`

```text
1. PI enabled
2. PRACT
3. Metadata size
4. PRCHK and STC
5. Status
```

**Question answered:** First determine whether namespace PI is enabled, then choose a processing branch by command direction and metadata size. Evaluate checking bits and special disable values afterward.

**Supporting Figures:** Figure 11, Figure 12, Figure 174, Figure 175, Figure 176

**Sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.1.5; 5.3.2-5.3.3, printed pp. 21-22,141-152, PDF pp. 21-22,141-152

### Visual 31: NVM behavior under ANA and Reservations

**View type:** `architecture`

```text
1. Namespace
2. ANA state
3. Reservation type
4. Holder and registrant
5. Command permission
```

**Question answered:** Check namespace access state separately from access permissions; path state does not establish reservation ownership.

**Supporting Figures:** Figure 141, Figure 199

**Sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §5.1; 5.11, printed pp. 119,172-173, PDF pp. 119,172-173

### Visual 32: LBA Migration Queue and change tracking

**View type:** `architecture`

```text
1. Track Send
2. Changes take effect
3. Range entries
4. Phase and sequence
5. Full or stop
```

**Question answered:** The queue records changed ranges and sequence markers rather than complete new data. The host still retrieves data with appropriate I/O and handles the logging-stop boundary caused by a full queue.

**Supporting Figures:** Figure 194

**Sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §4.1.8; 5.7, printed pp. 113-114,162-164, PDF pp. 113-114,162-164

### Visual 33: NVM rules for Sanitize and Media Verification

**View type:** `architecture`

```text
1. Target and state
2. LID81h
3. Allocation
4. Verification Read
5. Result interpretation
```

**Question answered:** Identify target, operation state, and allocation before deciding what can be verified. The initiating CQE and completion of the sanitize operation require different evidence.

**Supporting Figures:** Figure 200, Figure 201

**Sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §4.1.7; 5.12, printed pp. 113,173-175, PDF pp. 113,173-175

### Visual 34: NVM alignment constraints for Key Per I/O

**View type:** `architecture`

```text
1. Capability
2. Namespace enablement
3. CETYPE and CEV
4. KPIODAAG
5. Status
```

**Question answered:** Determine applicability from KPIOCAP and namespace status before decoding the CETYPE/CEV command extension. This NVM supplement does not fully define key creation or management.

**Supporting Figures:** 

**Sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §5.5; 4.1.5, printed pp. 91-92,105,160, PDF pp. 91-92,105,160

### Visual 35: NVM units and priorities for Streams

**View type:** `architecture`

```text
1. SWS blocks
2. SGS multiplier
3. Stream granularity
4. Namespace hints
5. Workload
```

**Question answered:** Use two size levels: Stream Write Size and the larger stream granularity. They may be integer multiples of namespace hints, but this is not guaranteed for every namespace.

**Supporting Figures:** Figure 152

**Sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §5.2.2.3; 5.13, printed pp. 128-129,175, PDF pp. 128-129,175

### Visual 36: Memory-based resource export template

**View type:** `architecture`

```text
1. Underlying capability
2. Template and TR
3. IDs 0 and 1
4. Set once
5. Reported interface
```

**Question answered:** The template compatibility interface and underlying device capabilities are separate layers. Check namespace-format compatibility, then configure limits no greater than underlying capabilities; do not advertise capabilities the template does not permit.

**Supporting Figures:** Figure 183, Figure 184, Figure 185, Figure 186, Figure 187, Figure 188, Figure 189, Figure 190

**Sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §5.4.1-5.4.1.1, printed pp. 152-159, PDF pp. 152-159

### Visual 37: Exported-state length and consistency

**View type:** `architecture`

```text
1. Current features
2. CP evidence
3. NVMECSS dwords
4. Bounds
5. Nested VER
```

**Question answered:** Read the fixed 64-byte header, then validate variable length and suspension evidence. Configuration state and runtime state differ in purpose and setting constraints; do not share their payload parsers.

## Mental Model and complete teaching path

The modules follow engineering causality rather than specification-section order. Related Figures return at the point where they support the flow.

### Module 01: Reading map and units

**Explanation.** This course follows namespaces and formats through command completion, integrity, and management evidence. Use four sessions of roughly 25 minutes for the main path, with figure worksheets and questions for further study. Chapter 1 terminology and reference conventions are included.

```text
Namespace
  ↓
Format
  ↓
Command
  ↓
Completion
  ↓
Evidence
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| LBADS | data bytes = 2^LBADS | Add MS to obtain logical block size |
| Format Index | Selects both LBAF and ELBAF | Data size alone is insufficient |
| Specification family | Base defines common mechanisms | Dependencies carry separate Base citations |

**Informative example.** With LBADS=0Ch and MS=16, data occupies 4096 bytes and the complete logical block 4112 bytes. FID 28h configures limits while LID 28h reports the capability graph, despite their equal numbers.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Worked values are teaching examples, not required device capabilities. Keep the different strengths of should, may, and shall.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §1.1-1.6; 4.1.3.9; 4.1.4.8; 4.1.5, printed pp. 9-12,73-75,79-83, PDF pp. 9-12,73-75,79-83

**Related Figures:** Figure 1, Figure 2

### Module 02: Namespace capacity and allocation

**Explanation.** Separate logical address space from allocated resources before considering writes and deallocation. Returned data and allocation state answer different questions.

```text
NSID
  ↓
NSZE
  ↓
NCAP
  ↓
NUSE
  ↓
Allocation
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| NSZE | Valid LBAs run from 0 to NSZE−1 | Out-of-range differs from capacity exhaustion |
| THINP | Requires NUSE tracking when supported | Without support NUSE may remain NCAP |
| Allocation | Write, the Copy destination, and WU allocate | Read/Verify do not change deallocation state |

**Informative example.** NSZE=1000, NCAP=800, NUSE=600 can describe a valid thin namespace. LBA 900 is addressable, but additional allocation remains subject to the 800-block capacity.

**Common mistake / debugging.** ANA state can zero reported NUSE/NVMCAP; those zeros alone do not establish data deletion.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.1.1; 4.1.5.1, printed pp. 13-14,85-93, PDF pp. 13-14,85-93

**Related Figures:** Figure 123

### Module 03: Ordering and Compare-and-Write

**Explanation.** First establish the ordering requirement, then decide whether conditional updating is needed. A fused operation protects comparison and update of the same LBA range, with atomic-size limits checked separately.

```text
Host dependency
  ↓
Compare
  ↓
Match gate
  ↓
Write
  ↓
Two CQEs
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| Ordinary I/O | Read/Write completion order for one LBA is not guaranteed | Use host completion dependencies |
| Fused pair | Compare and Write use the same range | A mismatch should be rejected |
| ACWU / NACWU | Bounds the fused atomic update | Atomic boundaries also apply |

**Informative example.** For “replace A with B only if A is still present,” an independent Compare followed by Write permits an intervening write. A fused pair within its size and boundary limits provides the conditional atomic update.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Write failure does not retroactively change the Compare completion status; inspect both CQEs.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.1.2-2.1.3, printed pp. 14-15, PDF pp. 14-15

**Related Figures:** Figure 3

### Module 04: Normal, power-fail, and multiple atomicity

**Explanation.** Read size, starting alignment, NSABP, and MAM together. Atomicity and persistence on nonvolatile media are separate checks; FUA/Flush do not establish ordering for other commands.

```text
NSABP
  ↓
Decode size
  ↓
Check boundaries
  ↓
MAM or single
  ↓
Failure outcome
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| AWUN / AWUPF | Sizes use zero-based encoding | AWUPF does not exceed AWUN |
| NABO / NABSN / NABSPF | Boundaries occur at offset + k × size | Decode each field and its unreported cases |
| MAM | Each atomic subrange has its own guarantee | Fused operations still use Single mode |
| FID 0Ah.DN | DN=1 releases normal-atomicity requirements | Power-fail guarantees remain |

**Informative example.** For decoded boundary size 8 blocks and offset zero, a 12-block write starting at LBA 4 splits into [4..7] and [8..15]. Under MAM each part is atomic, not one transaction. Raw AWUN=7h represents eight blocks.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Do not copy the §3.3.2.2 example equating NAWUN=8h with eight blocks: distinguish raw zero-based fields from decoded example sizes. Failed writes may still complete DMA, so buffer transfer completion is not media success.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.1.4; 4.1.3.4; 5.9, printed pp. 15-21,66-67,165, PDF pp. 15-21,66-67,165

**Related Figures:** Figure 4, Figure 5, Figure 6, Figure 7, Figure 8, Figure 9, Figure 10

### Module 05: Capabilities, opcodes, and status

**Explanation.** Build a command/Feature/log capability matrix starting from controller type. A data pointer may reference user data or merely control descriptors.

```text
Controller type
  ↓
Capability
  ↓
Opcode and NSID
  ↓
SCT plus SC
  ↓
Recovery
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| Read 02h / Write 01h | Mandatory I/O commands | Administrative controllers do not process I/O |
| Get LBA Status 86h | Optional Admin command | Capability belongs to I/O controllers |
| SC 80h | SCT distinguishes LBA Out of Range and other meanings | Record opcode, NSID, SCT, SC, and DNR |
| FID / LID | 05h and 0Ah are mandatory NVM Features | Feature support differs from Persistent Event Log recording |

**Informative example.** Copy opcode 19h has low bits 01b because the host supplies source descriptors; it does not require the host to retransmit all user data being copied.

**Common mistake / debugging.** NSID FFFF FFFFh is not accepted by every command; Figure 22 permits it only for the specifically noted Flush/Cancel paths.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.2; 3.1; 3.3, printed pp. 22-27, PDF pp. 22-27

**Related Figures:** Figure 13, Figure 14, Figure 15, Figure 16, Figure 17, Figure 18, Figure 19, Figure 20, Figure 22

### Module 06: Read/Write data and completion

**Explanation.** Check range, buffer, PI, and completion separately to distinguish addressing errors, format mismatches, and media failures.

```text
Range
  ↓
Buffer layout
  ↓
PI and FUA
  ↓
Execute
  ↓
CQE
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| CDW10 / CDW11 | Low/high 32 bits of SLBA | NLB=0 still requests one block |
| CDW12 | LR, FUA, PRINFO, STC, CETYPE, NLB | The DTYPE area is reserved for Read |
| CDW13 | CETYPE selects DSM or CEV interpretation | Write also carries DTYPE/DSPEC |
| MPTR | Used for separate metadata | Do not split metadata between both mechanisms |

**Informative example.** With SLBA=100, NLB=7, LBADS=12, and no metadata, Read covers 100..107 and 32768 bytes. An FUA Read commits the corresponding data before retrieving it from media; the host still orders dependent Writes.

**Common mistake / debugging.** On CQE failure retain SCT/SC and the range; FUA or successful DMA does not replace the completion result. With nonzero CETYPE, low CDW13 bits cannot be decoded as DSM hints.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §3.3.4; 3.3.6, printed pp. 48-51,53-56, PDF pp. 48-51,53-56

**Related Figures:** Figure 50, Figure 51, Figure 52, Figure 53, Figure 54, Figure 55, Figure 56, Figure 57, Figure 58, Figure 59, Figure 67, Figure 68, Figure 69, Figure 70, Figure 71, Figure 72, Figure 73, Figure 74, Figure 75, Figure 76

### Module 07: Compare and Verify answer different questions

**Explanation.** Expected-content comparison, integrity verification, and ordinary Read provide different evidence. Compare excludes PI from metadata comparison and checks PI separately as requested.

```text
Question
  ↓
Compare or Verify
  ↓
PRACT and checks
  ↓
Size gate
  ↓
Status
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| Compare | A miscompare returns Compare Failure | PI can be checked on both host and media paths |
| Verify | No data-buffer transfer | Verified data still counts toward Data Units Read |
| VSL / NVMVFYS | The variant selects recommended size or a hard limit | Nonzero VSL uses 2^n × minimum page size |

**Informative example.** To determine whether stored contents equal zero, Compare can use a zero-filled expected buffer. Successful Verify establishes this integrity check, not that the contents equal zero.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Verify with PRACT=1 returns Invalid Field in Command. Treating Verify as a zero-length Read or Compare as a data-return command leads to incorrect buffer setup.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §3.3.1; 3.3.5, printed pp. 27-30,51-53, PDF pp. 27-30,51-53

**Related Figures:** Figure 23, Figure 24, Figure 25, Figure 26, Figure 27, Figure 28, Figure 29, Figure 30, Figure 31, Figure 60, Figure 61, Figure 62, Figure 63, Figure 64, Figure 65, Figure 66

### Module 08: Copy: source descriptors, contiguous destination, partial failure

**Explanation.** Calculate the expanded destination range before checking formats, limits, overlap, and atomicity. Copy reduces host data movement but is not an unconditional transaction.

```text
Descriptors
  ↓
Destination range
  ↓
Limits and overlap
  ↓
Copy
  ↓
Partial-result CQE
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| NR / NLB | Source count and per-range block count are zero-based | Check MSRC, MSSRL, and MCL |
| FCO | Formats 2h/3h can request fast copy only | Inspect DNR after Fast Copy Not Possible |
| Overlap | Formats 2h/3h prohibit source/destination overlap within one namespace | Formats 0h/1h need their separate overlap rules |
| NVMCSA | Revision 1.3 treats the destination as one write command | MAM, size, and boundary limits still apply |

**Informative example.** Two descriptors with NLB=3 and SDLBA=100 write 100..103 and 104..107: eight blocks total. DW0=1 does not prove that the second or any later range is entirely unmodified.

**Common mistake / debugging.** FCO constrains the method, not the latency of every operation. Atomicity value FFFFh represents 65536 blocks; Copy can exceed that size, so it does not make all Copy commands atomic.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §3.3.2, printed pp. 30-44, PDF pp. 30-44

**Related Figures:** Figure 32, Figure 33, Figure 34, Figure 35, Figure 36, Figure 37, Figure 38, Figure 39, Figure 40, Figure 41, Figure 42, Figure 43

### Module 09: Copy PI compatibility and transformation

**Explanation.** Classify whether source and destination use PI, then choose PRINFOR.PRACT and PRINFOW.PRACT. Every source must fit the selected mode.

```text
Source PI
  ↓
Destination PI
  ↓
Matching or corresponding
  ↓
PRACT pair
  ↓
Check and transform
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| PI → PI, 0/0 | Matching formats: pass-through | Checking remains controlled by check bits |
| PI → PI, 1/1 | Matching formats: replace | Check the read path and generate write PI |
| No PI → PI | Corresponding formats and write PRACT=1: insert | Destination metadata cannot include other content |
| PI → No PI | Corresponding formats and read PRACT=1: strip | Source metadata must be PI-only |

**Informative example.** A 4096+8-byte namespace with 16b PI can copy to 4096+0 bytes under the corresponding-format conditions. A 4096+16-byte source with eight extra metadata bytes cannot use that strip exception.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Sections 5.3.2.5.1/.2 interchange references to Figures 177–180. Cross-check their actual captions with §3.3.2.4.2: 0/0 passes PI through and 1/1 replaces it.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §3.3.2.3-3.3.2.4; 5.3.2.5, printed pp. 40-43,146-150, PDF pp. 40-43,146-150

**Related Figures:** Figure 177, Figure 178, Figure 179, Figure 180, Figure 181, Figure 182

### Module 10: Dataset Management and three processing limits

**Explanation.** Determine whether each block satisfies all three limits before applying NVMDSMSV. Separate range/hint validity, attribute processing obligations, and actual media actions.

```text
16-byte ranges
  ↓
Three limits
  ↓
NVMDSMSV
  ↓
Process hints
  ↓
Allocation evidence
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| AD / IDW / IDR | Deallocate/integral-write/integral-read hints | Combinations are permitted |
| Limits nonzero, variant=0 | Exceeding a limit returns Command Size Limit Exceeded | All fitting blocks require attribute processing |
| Limits nonzero, variant=1 | Should process the portion satisfying the limits | Do not report Size Limit Exceeded for this reason |
| All limits=0 | Variant=1: no limits reported; variant=0: unsupported | All three fields must be zero or all nonzero |

**Informative example.** With DMRL=2, DMSL=1048, ranges of 1024 and 512 blocks, and a nonrestrictive DMRSL, variant=1 admits the first range and 24 blocks of the second. This does not guarantee deallocation of 1048 blocks.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Do not reuse the Write NLB encoder for DSM LLB. Zero-based encoding undercounts the range by one; LLB=0 does not mean one block.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §3.3.3, printed pp. 44-48, PDF pp. 44-48

**Related Figures:** Figure 44, Figure 45, Figure 46, Figure 47, Figure 48, Figure 49

### Module 11: Reading deallocated/unwritten blocks

**Explanation.** First determine whether successful reading is permitted, then interpret returned bytes. Allocation status, DRB, and PI have separate conditions.

```text
DAE
  ↓
DULBE
  ↓
DRB
  ↓
PI values
  ↓
Deterministic read
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| DAE / DULBE | DAE is capability; DULBE is enablement | DULBE defaults to zero |
| DRB=000b | Does not mean arbitrary old data | Section 3.3.3.2.1 limits it to zeros or FFh |
| PI after deallocation | Tag bytes return FFh; Guard is FFh or CRC | Use DLFEAT.GDS |

**Informative example.** One zero-filled Read does not prove successful sanitize; it may reflect DRB on deallocated blocks. Conversely, a DULBE error alone does not establish a media defect.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Successful Read/Verify does not reallocate the block; writing changes that state.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §3.3.3.2.1; 4.1.3.3, printed pp. 47-48,66, PDF pp. 47-48,66

**Related Figures:** 

### Module 12: Write Uncorrectable, Write Zeroes, and whole-namespace zeroing

**Explanation.** Neither command transfers a host user-data payload, but both change namespace semantics. Identify range mode before checking PI and size limits.

```text
Operation
  ↓
Range or NSZ
  ↓
PI and limits
  ↓
Execute
  ↓
LBACZ and status
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| Write Uncorrectable | Marks blocks so later reads can report Unrecovered Read Error | Interpret WUSL with NVMWUSV |
| Write Zeroes PI | PRCHK=000b, STC=0 | PRACT=1 is recommended for valid PI |
| WZSL / WZDSL | Select the applicable limit using DEAC | Neither limit applies with NSZ=1 |
| LBACZ | One on a successful NSZ command reports the entire namespace | Zero reports the specified range |

**Informative example.** Successful Completion with NSZ=1 but LBACZ=0 means only the range was zeroed. An older controller may ignore unsupported NSZ; command success alone does not establish whole-namespace zeroing.

**Common mistake / debugging.** DEAC=0 does not prohibit deallocation: the controller may still deallocate when zero-read conditions hold. A failed Write Zeroes can also have cleared some contents.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §3.3.7-3.3.8, printed pp. 56-61, PDF pp. 56-61

**Related Figures:** Figure 77, Figure 78, Figure 79, Figure 80, Figure 81, Figure 82, Figure 83, Figure 84, Figure 85, Figure 86, Figure 87, Figure 88, Figure 89

### Module 13: Format, Host Behavior, and extended LBAs

**Explanation.** Formatting can change block counts and field applicability; re-identify before constructing buffers. Do not confuse capability lists with the active format.

```text
ELBAS
  ↓
LBAFEE
  ↓
LBAF and ELBAF
  ↓
PI and metadata
  ↓
Re-identify
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| PI / PIL | PI=0 disables protection; 1/2/3 select its type | This revision requires PIL=0, placing PI last |
| MSET | One: extended LBA; zero: separate metadata | Ignored when MS=0 |
| LBAFEE | FID 16h byte 2, valid values zero/one | ELBAS also gates extended formats |
| STS | Format cannot freely change STS to a new nonzero value | Namespace creation can establish a new configuration |

**Informative example.** For 64b Guard with MS=16, first check ELBAS, LBAFEE=1, the corresponding LBAF/ELBAF, and PI capability. Setting Format PI=1 alone does not select 64b Guard.

**Common mistake / debugging.** PI types 1/2/3 and Guard widths 16/32/64 are separate dimensions. NSZE/NCAP can change after formatting, and old LBA Range Type hints may need updating.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §4.1.2; 4.1.3.7, printed pp. 62-63,68-69, PDF pp. 62-63,68-69

**Related Figures:** Figure 91, Figure 101

### Module 14: Basic Feature scopes and exceptions

**Explanation.** Identify scope, units, and saveability when reading Features. Get, Set, and Supported Capabilities responses do not share one payload interpretation.

```text
Scope
  ↓
Units
  ↓
Select or Set
  ↓
Persistence
  ↓
Returned value
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| FID 03h | 4096-byte contiguous buffer; up to 64 64-byte entries | NUM is zero-based; each new Set replaces prior information |
| FID 05h.TLER | 100 ms units, timed from error-recovery start | Zero means no timeout; applies to LR-enabled commands |
| FID 03h attributes | Hide/Overwriteable are host-use hints | They do not establish security isolation or data protection |
| FID 02h extension | Idle-exit reference is an NPWG-sized Read | Other commands may exceed that latency limit |

**Informative example.** TLER=5 gives an error-recovery limit of 500 ms, not a 500 ms deadline measured from SQ submission. LBA Range Type NUM=0 represents one entry.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Figure 92 persistence applies only to nonsaveable Features; saveable ones follow saved/default rules. A controller need not validate every LBA Range Type field, so successful Set does not establish that all ranges are sensible.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §4.1.3.1-4.1.3.4, printed pp. 64-67, PDF pp. 64-67

**Related Figures:** Figure 92, Figure 93, Figure 94, Figure 95, Figure 96, Figure 97, Figure 98

### Module 15: Identify: multiple structures for one namespace

**Explanation.** Write down the roles of CNS, CSI, NSID, and Format Index for each query. Zero-filled results have different meanings across queries and do not always mean absent or unsupported.

```text
CNS and CSI
  ↓
NSID or FIDX
  ↓
Independent structure
  ↓
NVM structures
  ↓
Combine capabilities
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| CNS 00h / 05h | Basic/extended NVM namespace fields | FLBAS selects the active FIDX; MC/DPC are capabilities |
| CNS 01h / 06h | Common-location AWUN fields and NVM-specific limits | 06h VSL/WZSL fields require variant bits |
| CNS 11h / 1Bh | Allocated-namespace information | Different from active-namespace queries |
| CNS 09h / 0Ah | Capability queries by FIDX | Common=No fields are zeroed |
| CNS 16h | Namespace granularity list | GDM determines descriptor-to-format mapping |

**Informative example.** For NSID=7, read FLBAS and use that index in both LBAF and ELBAF. To query capabilities of FIDX=3 before creation, use 09h/0Ah, CSI=0, NSID=0, FIDX=3, plus common capabilities from CNS08h.

**Common mistake / debugging.** The “zoned namespace” wording in §4.1.5.10.1 conflicts with its NVM context. This course interprets it as the NVM namespace under CSI=00h and retains the source location for review.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §4.1.5, printed pp. 83-110, PDF pp. 83-110

**Related Figures:** Figure 122, Figure 126, Figure 129, Figure 130, Figure 131

### Module 16: LBAF, ELBAF, and unique-attribute formats

**Explanation.** The basic entry gives data/metadata sizes and relative performance; the extended entry gives PI format and Storage Tag allocation. Query unique-attribute entries individually instead of assuming common capabilities.

```text
NLBAF plus NULBAF
  ↓
Format Index
  ↓
LBAF
  ↓
ELBAF
  ↓
Availability
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| LBAF | LBADS, MS, RP | RP is a relative class for a specified workload |
| ELBAF | PIF, QPIF, STS | QPIF applies only to qualified type |
| FLBAS | FIDXU and FIDXL form the index | MTELBA is a separate metadata bit |
| NULBAF | Appended after common formats | 09h/0Ah retrieve individual capabilities |

**Informative example.** Raw NLBAF=3 and NULBAF=2 give four common formats and two unique-attribute formats: six total, indices 0..5. Figure 192 uses conceptual counts; do not substitute raw NLBAF without decoding it.

**Common mistake / debugging.** LBADS=9 means 512 bytes and LBADS=12 means 4096 bytes. The §5.3.1.4.1 example equating LBADS=0 with 512 bytes is a source inconsistency and must not drive command construction.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §4.1.5.1; 4.1.5.3; 5.6, printed pp. 85-94,96-102,160-162, PDF pp. 85-94,96-102,160-162

**Related Figures:** Figure 124, Figure 125, Figure 127, Figure 128, Figure 192, Figure 193

### Module 17: Namespace creation: format, mask, granularity

**Explanation.** Query Format Index capabilities before filling host-specified fields; do not use an entire unmodified Identify Namespace structure as the create payload.

```text
Format capability
  ↓
NSZE and NCAP
  ↓
PI and LBSTM
  ↓
Placement handles
  ↓
Create result
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| NSZE / NCAP | Values are specified in logical blocks | Convert before comparing with byte granularities |
| LBSTM | Must satisfy PIC/PIFA masking constraints | Violations return Invalid Field in Command |
| GDM / ND | GDM=0 uses descriptor zero for all formats | ND is zero-based |
| Completion | Successful creation includes the requested formatting | Attachment is a separate management action |

**Informative example.** With NSG=NCG=1 MiB and logical block size 4096, NSZE=NCAP=256 makes the allocation fully addressable. Choosing 257 may leave extra unaddressable allocation under the hints, but that alone is not a rejection reason.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Masking Not Supported requires all significant Storage Tag mask bits to be one, not zero. Placement fields do not acquire enabled-FDP semantics when FDP is unsupported or disabled.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §4.1.6; 4.1.5.8; 5.8, printed pp. 108,110-113,165, PDF pp. 108,110-113,165

**Related Figures:** Figure 132, Figure 133, Figure 134

### Module 18: FDP: placement, RUHs, and observable data

**Explanation.** Creation establishes placement relationships; handle status describes operation, and statistics/events explain later media movement. These evidence types are not interchangeable.

```text
Create placement
  ↓
PID and RUHID
  ↓
Handle status
  ↓
Statistics
  ↓
Media event
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| NPHNDLS | At most 128 and no more than the configuration RUH count | Zero invokes controller-selection and sharing rules |
| EARUTR / RUAMW | Estimated remaining seconds / writable logical blocks | EARUTR=0 means unreported; not a lifetime guarantee |
| LID 22h | HBMW/MBMW include the specified NVM write-class commands | Includes Copy destination, Zeroes, and Uncorrectable |
| LID 23h event 0h | LBAV governs LBA validity | NLBAM=FFFFh means at least FFFFh |

**Informative example.** If two namespaces share RUH 5 and one uses FIDX=2, creating the other with FIDX=3 violates the shared-RUH Format Index rule even if both have 4 KiB data blocks.

**Common mistake / debugging.** The LBA in a Media Reallocated event is one member of the moved set, not a complete list; ignore it when LBAV=0.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §3.2.1; 4.1.4.6-4.1.4.7; 4.1.6.3, printed pp. 26,79,110-113, PDF pp. 26,79,110-113

**Related Figures:** Figure 21, Figure 116

### Module 19: NVM extensions to AER, SMART, and error records

**Explanation.** Use events to direct investigation, then decode logs using their scope and command-set definitions. Classify commands correctly when interpreting statistics instead of guessing from opcode names.

```text
Notice enable
  ↓
AER
  ↓
Log scope
  ↓
Validity and units
  ↓
Correlate evidence
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| LBASIN / RLCCN | FID0Bh bits 13/22 | Enable LBA Status / Rate Limiting notices |
| SMART units | Convert to 512-byte units, then apply Base counter encoding | One 4 KiB block is not one Data Unit |
| Read categories | Data Units Read includes Verify; Host Read includes Copy | Compare and Read belong to both categories |
| Persistent Event 06h | Create/single-delete records contain FLBAS and DPS | Both fields are reserved for delete-all |

**Informative example.** A Self-test record with FLBA=100 and valid=1 identifies one failing LBA, not a clean bill of health for all others. Error Information’s “lowest LBA” semantics cannot be applied to FLBA.

**Common mistake / debugging.** The Rate Limiting log uses CSI, while most other listed logs do not; do not mix command-set definitions for the same LID.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §1.4.2; 4.1.1; 4.1.3.5; 4.1.4.1-4.1.4.4, printed pp. 10-11,62,67,75-77, PDF pp. 10-11,62,67,75-77

**Related Figures:** Figure 90, Figure 99, Figure 109, Figure 110, Figure 111, Figure 112

### Module 20: LBA Status: notices, scans, and recovery

**Explanation.** Potentially unrecoverable does not mean every block necessarily fails to read. Identify ATYPE, check buffer capacity and completion condition, then arrange data recovery.

```text
LID 0Eh
  ↓
ATYPE
  ↓
Range and MNDW
  ↓
CMPC and descriptors
  ↓
Recover and recheck
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| MNDW / RL | MNDW is zero-based dwords; RL=0 runs through NSZE−1 | RL=0 does not query one block |
| NLSD / CMPC | Actual descriptor count / completion reason | CMPC=1 means more data or incomplete scan; 2 means complete |
| LSIPI / LSIRI | 100 ms units; host cannot change the poll interval | Set returns the closest supported value |
| RAE / LSGC | Read chunks with RAE=1; RAE=0 clears the event and allows updates | Reread the header and check generation |
| TLBAAG | 02h may report allocation at a larger granularity | A mixed unit is reported allocated as a whole |

**Informative example.** NLSLNE=0 with nonzero ESTULB is not an all-clear: examine the full ranges of attached namespaces. Recover suspect LBAs from another reliable source and rewrite them; later queries remove successfully rewritten entries unless newly detected again.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Command success with CMPC=1 does not mean the whole range was scanned. Log RNLB and detailed-descriptor NLB are zero-based, while NLSD is an actual count.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §4.1.3.6; 4.1.4.5; 4.2.1; 5.2.1, printed pp. 67-68,77-79,114-122, PDF pp. 67-68,77-79,114-122

**Related Figures:** Figure 100, Figure 113, Figure 114, Figure 115, Figure 135, Figure 136, Figure 137, Figure 138, Figure 139, Figure 140, Figure 142, Figure 143, Figure 144

### Module 21: Performance Characteristics attributes

**Explanation.** This Feature reports or manages performance attributes; its standard latency class is not a service guarantee for arbitrary workloads.

```text
Scope
  ↓
ATTRI
  ↓
Current default saved
  ↓
PAID and length
  ↓
Interpretation
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| R4KARL | Average-latency range for standardized 4 KiB random reads | 00h means unreported |
| MSVSPA / USVSPA | Saveable capacity / unused capacity | Indices can be noncontiguous |
| PAID / ATTRL | 128-bit identifier / valid vendor bytes | ATTRL is at most FE0h |
| RVSPA | Delete the saved value to return to default | The data-buffer contents are unused |

**Informative example.** R4KARL=0Eh means 50 μs ≤ average latency <100 μs, not 14 μs. When reading the C0h list, match ATTRTYP with Get SEL and use PAID to interpret vendor payloads.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Set with ATTRI=00h or C0h returns Invalid Field in Command. Vendor-byte meanings require a vendor definition and cannot be invented as standard fields.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §4.1.3.8, printed pp. 69-73, PDF pp. 69-73

**Related Figures:** Figure 102, Figure 103, Figure 104, Figure 105

### Module 22: Rate Limiting configuration fields

**Explanation.** Obtain supported targets from LID 28h, then check HLS/SLS and the soft-controller count. Record requested limits separately from attainable device capabilities.

```text
Supported targets
  ↓
HLS and SLS
  ↓
TGT and TID
  ↓
Limits and ratios
  ↓
Set and Get
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| TGT / TID | CDW11[23:16] / [15:0] | TGT=0 is the standard controller target |
| RLC | RLE bit15; RLM=0 Hard, 1 Soft | Soft support requires Hard support |
| BWSF | 0/1/2 = 1/10/100 MiB/s; 3/4/5 = 1/10/100 GiB/s | Multiply the value by the scale |
| WRIOPSR / WRBWR | Write numerator divided by read denominator | Every ratio component byte must be nonzero |

**Informative example.** BWSF=1 and TBWV=50 specify 500 MiB/s. WBWV/WIOPS govern writes, while total consumption is weighted by WRBWR/WRIOPSR; total limits are not simply read limits.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Limits for an unconfigured target are vendor-specific, not necessarily unlimited. The opening §5.10 references interchange Hard/Soft sections: 5.10.1 is Hard and 5.10.2 is Soft.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §4.1.3.9; 4.1.5.4; 5.10, printed pp. 73-75,106,165-168, PDF pp. 73-75,106,165-168

**Related Figures:** Figure 106, Figure 107, Figure 108

### Module 23: The Rate Limiting log is a capability graph

**Explanation.** Validate structure bounds before analyzing bandwidth bottlenecks. Port capability differs from shared Endurance Group capability; do not simply add all reported numbers.

```text
Header and GC
  ↓
Port offsets
  ↓
Controller offsets
  ↓
Shared storage nodes
  ↓
Bounds and bottleneck
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| LPL / offsets | Lengths and pointers use dword units | Byte offset = dword offset ×4 |
| NP / NC / NST | All are zero-based counts | NNSMAD is an actual count |
| SC / SI | Subsystem/domain/EG/namespace and its ID | Interpret scope and avoid double-counting shared nodes |
| RLMA | Maximum read/write bandwidth/IOPS | Relevant size/queue-depth workload conditions apply |

**Informative example.** Two PCIe ports may share one Endurance Group. If controller 0 consumes all EG bandwidth, the extra port does not create more media bandwidth for controller 1. Both controllers may reference one descriptor for identical EG access capabilities.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Examples in Figures 196/198 contain inconsistent offsets, byte ranges, and LPL. This course redraws the relationships and checks offset×4, descriptor length, and LPL bounds instead of treating the examples as executable binary fixtures.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §4.1.4.8; 5.10.3, printed pp. 79-83,168-172, PDF pp. 79-83,168-172

**Related Figures:** Figure 117, Figure 118, Figure 119, Figure 120, Figure 121, Figure 195, Figure 196, Figure 197, Figure 198

### Module 24: Hard/Soft modes and token-bucket examples

**Explanation.** Interpret results using capability, configured limits, and actual demand. A configured ratio does not force a fixed throughput ratio at every instant; internal resources and workload still matter.

```text
Capabilities
  ↓
Configured limits
  ↓
Actual demand
  ↓
Token admission
  ↓
Completion
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| Hard | Proportional sharing under demand and resource shortage | A configured ceiling is not a performance floor |
| Soft | May consume unused capacity | Multiple soft targets share it in proportion to limits |
| Write tokens | Total bytes × WRBWR; write bytes; total IOPS × WRIOPSR; one write IOPS | Check each of four buckets |
| Read tokens | Total bytes and one total IOPS | Does not consume write-only buckets |

**Informative example.** Teaching setup: a 4 KiB Write with WRBWR=2 and WRIOPSR=3 consumes 8 KiB total-bandwidth, 4 KiB write-bandwidth, three total-IOPS, and one write-IOPS token. A 4 KiB Read consumes only 4 KiB total-bandwidth and one total-IOPS token.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Insufficient tokens defer commands rather than drop them. Partial processing is allowed, but completion cannot precede processing of the entire command.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §5.10.1-5.10.2; Appendix A, printed pp. 166-168,176-177, PDF pp. 166-168,176-177

**Related Figures:** Figure 202

### Module 25: Alignment, granularity, and performance hints

**Explanation.** Decode raw fields into blocks, then evaluate starting alignment and length granularity. Meeting only one can still cause read-modify-write.

```text
Support bits
  ↓
Decode units
  ↓
Align start
  ↓
Choose length
  ↓
Measure workload
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| NPWG / NPWA | Meet both length and start recommendations | First check NSFEAT.OPTPERF |
| NPRG / NPRA / NORS | Guide read optimization | First check OPTRPERF |
| NPDG / NPDGL | Alternative deallocate-granularity fields | Select via OPTPERF; Large fields do not universally add one |
| NOIOB / NABO | Optimal I/O boundary differs from atomic offset | I/O can be split to satisfy multiple conditions |

**Informative example.** With decoded NPWG=8 and NPWA=8, writing LBAs 8..15 meets both. Writing 9..16 also has eight blocks but crosses two units and may require reading old data at both ends.

**Common mistake / debugging.** The source’s read-modify-write diagrams illustrate a possible mechanism, not a mandatory internal implementation on every SSD. Reformatting can invalidate old alignment hints.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §5.2.2, printed pp. 122-129, PDF pp. 122-129

**Related Figures:** Figure 145, Figure 146, Figure 147, Figure 148, Figure 149, Figure 150, Figure 151

### Module 26: Metadata transfer and PI placement

**Explanation.** Metadata need not consist entirely of PI. Mark data, non-PI metadata, and PI separately before computing host-buffer size and CRC coverage.

```text
Namespace format
  ↓
Data region
  ↓
Metadata region
  ↓
PI suffix
  ↓
Buffer lengths
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| Extended LBA | DPTR addresses interleaved data+metadata | MSET/MTELBA reflect the selection |
| Separate buffer | DPTR addresses data; MPTR addresses metadata | PRP metadata is physically contiguous; SGL metadata may be scattered |
| PI location | Valid current formats put PI at the metadata end | CRC covers preceding non-PI metadata |

**Informative example.** For eight blocks, data=4096, MS=16, PRACT=0: the extended buffer is 32896 bytes; separate buffers are 32768 data bytes and 128 metadata bytes.

**Common mistake / debugging.** PI placement at the end and separate-versus-extended metadata are independent choices; DIF/DIX terminology does not replace namespace-format settings.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.1.6; 5.2.3; 5.3, printed pp. 22,129-131, PDF pp. 22,129-131

**Related Figures:** Figure 153, Figure 154

### Module 27: 16/32/64b Guard and qualified PI

**Explanation.** Select the format with PIF; only PIF=11b delegates Guard width to QPIF, subject to QPIFS and STMLA. DPS separately selects protection type.

```text
DPS type
  ↓
PIF or QPIF
  ↓
Guard size
  ↓
STS split
  ↓
Mask capability
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| 16b Guard | 2-byte Guard + 2-byte App + 4-byte space | STS=0..32 |
| 32b Guard | 4-byte Guard + 2-byte App + 10-byte space | STS=16..64 |
| 64b Guard | 8-byte Guard + 2-byte App + 6-byte space | STS=0..48 |
| STMLA | Bit masking / byte masking / no masking | Qualified type and QPIFS determine applicability |

**Informative example.** With 64b Guard and STS=18, the high 18 bits of the 48-bit space form Storage Tag and the low 30 bits form Reference Tag. Total PI remains 16 bytes; increasing STS does not enlarge it.

**Common mistake / debugging.** This revision defines qualified type, so PIF=11b is not universally reserved. Reference Tag is absent when STS consumes the entire space; Storage Tag is absent when STS=0.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §5.3.1; 4.1.5.3, printed pp. 97-102,130-138, PDF pp. 97-102,130-138

**Related Figures:** Figure 155, Figure 156, Figure 157, Figure 159, Figure 164, Figure 165

### Module 28: CRC parameters, bit order, and known vectors

**Explanation.** Check polynomial, initialization, reflection, final XOR, and storage order together. Validate known vectors before integrating a PI parser.

```text
Data and metadata
  ↓
Initialization
  ↓
Polynomial and reflection
  ↓
Final XOR
  ↓
Known vectors
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| CRC-16 | Guard CRC defined by SBC-4 | NVM does not support the optional DIX IP checksum |
| CRC-32C | Polynomial 1EDC6F41h | 4 KiB zero vector → 98F94189h |
| CRC-64/NVME | Reflected-register example 123456789 → AE8B14860A799888h | 4 KiB zero vector → 6482D367EB22B64Eh |
| Coverage | Data plus metadata preceding PI | Exclude PI itself |

**Informative example.** The CRC-64 result for 4 KiB of FFh is C0DDBA7302ECA3ACh. If the zero vector passes but the incrementing-byte vector fails, inspect byte/bit order rather than changing the polynomial to fit.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Figure 161 lists Check=11199E506128D175h; a conventional LSB-first register computes AE8B14860A799888h for 123456789. They are 64-bit reversals. All four Figure 163 4 KiB vectors directly match that register result. State this representation discrepancy rather than changing the polynomial to fit one Check value. CRC is not cryptographic authentication.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §5.3.1.1-5.3.1.3, printed pp. 131-137, PDF pp. 131-137

**Related Figures:** Figure 158, Figure 160, Figure 161, Figure 162, Figure 163

### Module 29: Packing Storage/Reference Tags into Dwords

**Explanation.** Determine total space width, split the tags, then pack command Dwords. Similar names do not make Write values interchangeable with Read expected values.

```text
PI space width
  ↓
STS
  ↓
Storage and reference
  ↓
CDW2 and CDW3
  ↓
CDW14
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| 16b Guard, STS=0 | CDW14 contains the 32-bit reference | CDW2/3 are ignored for this tag |
| 32b Guard, STS=32 | CDW2 low16 + CDW3 high16 carry Storage | CDW3 low16 + CDW14 carry the 48-bit Reference |
| 64b Guard, STS=18 | CDW3 low16 + CDW14 high2 carry Storage | CDW14 low30 carry Reference |

**Informative example.** For 64b Guard, STS=18, Storage Tag=0x12345, Reference Tag=0x2A: CDW3 low16=0x48D1 and CDW14=(1<<30)|0x2A=0x4000002A. Read uses expected tags in the same layout.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Figure 171 gives a CDW3 Storage Tag range overlapping the next row. Figures 166 and 170 support interpreting it as high16; this is an explicitly identified engineering interpretation of a source inconsistency.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §5.3.1.4, printed pp. 137-141, PDF pp. 137-141

**Related Figures:** Figure 166, Figure 167, Figure 168, Figure 169, Figure 170, Figure 171, Figure 172, Figure 173

### Module 30: Combining PRACT with PRCHK/STC

**Explanation.** First determine whether namespace PI is enabled, then choose a processing branch by command direction and metadata size. Evaluate checking bits and special disable values afterward.

```text
PI enabled
  ↓
PRACT
  ↓
Metadata size
  ↓
PRCHK and STC
  ↓
Status
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| Write, PRACT=1 | Insert PI when MS=PI; replace it when MS>PI | This generation branch ignores PRCHK/STC |
| Read, PRACT=1 | Perform requested checks; strip only when MS=PI | MS>PI still returns metadata including PI |
| Type 1 / Type 2 | Reference increments per block | Type1 initial value must match relevant low SLBA bits |
| Type 3 | Should not compare a computed reference | An RTCHK rejection uses Invalid Protection Information |
| Disable sentinels | Type 1/2 disable all PI checks when Application Tag=FFFFh; Type 3 additionally requires an all-ones Reference Tag, if defined | Overrides PRCHK/STC settings |
| Masks | A zero mask bit excludes comparison | Storage masking also obeys STMLA |

**Informative example.** For 16b Guard, MS=16, Read PRACT=1, the host still receives 16 metadata bytes. With MS=8 it receives data only. The same PRACT value produces different buffer lengths under different MS.

**Common mistake / debugging.** STC here means Storage Tag Check, not Self-test Code. Both Compare input paths can perform PI checking, while PI bytes are excluded from ordinary metadata comparison.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §2.1.5; 5.3.2-5.3.3, printed pp. 21-22,141-152, PDF pp. 21-22,141-152

**Related Figures:** Figure 11, Figure 12, Figure 174, Figure 175, Figure 176

### Module 31: NVM behavior under ANA and Reservations

**Explanation.** Check namespace access state separately from access permissions; path state does not establish reservation ownership.

```text
Namespace
  ↓
ANA state
  ↓
Reservation type
  ↓
Holder and registrant
  ↓
Command permission
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| ANA Identify | NUSE/NVMCAP return zero in Inaccessible/Persistent Loss | This does not mean media was erased |
| ANA FID05h | Get is restricted in Inaccessible/Persistent Loss/Change | Use the corresponding ANA status |
| Write Exclusive / Exclusive Access | For nonholders, the former allows read-like commands; the latter conflicts with read-like and write-like commands | Nonholder write-like commands conflict for both |
| Registrants Only / All Registrants | Write Exclusive variants allow reads by anyone and writes by registrants; Exclusive Access variants allow reads/writes only by registrants | Copy checks each source as read and its destination as write |
| Reservations | Check the matrix for read-like/write-like commands | Holder, registrant, and type all matter |

**Informative example.** Two PCIe controllers of one SSD may share a namespace. Controller 1 can have an accessible path yet be unable to Write due to reservation type and its registration state; Read permissions require a separate matrix lookup.

**Common mistake / debugging.** A reservation does not universally block all nonholder I/O; types such as Write Exclusive and Exclusive Access have different read rules.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §5.1; 5.11, printed pp. 119,172-173, PDF pp. 119,172-173

**Related Figures:** Figure 141, Figure 199

### Module 32: LBA Migration Queue and change tracking

**Explanation.** The queue records changed ranges and sequence markers rather than complete new data. The host still retrieves data with appropriate I/O and handles the logging-stop boundary caused by a full queue.

```text
Track Send
  ↓
Changes take effect
  ↓
Range entries
  ↓
Phase and sequence
  ↓
Full or stop
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| LBACIR | 00: range; 01: whole namespace; 10: no range | Determine field validity first |
| ESA | 001 start/resume; 010 stop; 011 suspend; 111 full | Full means logging stopped |
| DLBA / CDQP | Deallocation flag / entry phase | DLBA=0 may still describe a deallocation-related change |
| RALBAS | ATYPE02h covers changes during the start command when supported | Start/stop markers need not precede Track Send CQE |

**Informative example.** Three sequential Writes may become one range entry, so entry count is not write-command count. After ESA=111b, the host cannot assume subsequent changes continue to be logged.

**Common mistake / debugging.** This lesson covers NVM LBA change tracking without expanding into other transport protocols or resource-export formats. Address queue capacity and consistency before restarting tracking.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §4.1.8; 5.7, printed pp. 113-114,162-164, PDF pp. 113-114,162-164

**Related Figures:** Figure 194

### Module 33: NVM rules for Sanitize and Media Verification

**Explanation.** Identify target, operation state, and allocation before deciding what can be verified. The initiating CQE and completion of the sanitize operation require different evidence.

```text
Target and state
  ↓
LID81h
  ↓
Allocation
  ↓
Verification Read
  ↓
Result interpretation
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| LID81h | Tracks operation status/progress | Successful initiation is not operation completion |
| Error Information | The NVM LBA field returns zero during sanitize | This NVM extension still obeys the Base command allowlist |
| Media Verification Read | PRCHK=000b, STC=0 | Requesting checking gives Invalid Field in Command |
| Allocated media | Return actual data if readable; error if unreadable | Qualifying reads return Successful Media Verification Read |

**Informative example.** In Media Verification, a Read without PI checking can ignore integrity errors when allocated media remains readable and return the specific success status. Repeated reads of one LBA may differ, so ordinary stable-value assumptions do not apply.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Zero-filled reads after sanitize are not sufficient proof of success, and not every method is expected to return zeros. Namespace and subsystem sanitize scopes are not interchangeable.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §4.1.7; 5.12, printed pp. 113,173-175, PDF pp. 113,173-175

**Related Figures:** Figure 200, Figure 201

### Module 34: NVM alignment constraints for Key Per I/O

**Explanation.** Determine applicability from KPIOCAP and namespace status before decoding the CETYPE/CEV command extension. This NVM supplement does not fully define key creation or management.

```text
Capability
  ↓
Namespace enablement
  ↓
CETYPE and CEV
  ↓
KPIODAAG
  ↓
Status
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| KPIOCAP | Support and subsystem/namespace scope | Do not rely on an enable bit alone |
| KPIOSNS / KPIOENS | Namespace support / enablement | Enable must be zero without support |
| KPIODAAG | Zero-based logical-block granularity | Both start and length must conform |

**Informative example.** Raw KPIODAAG=7 represents eight-block granularity. SLBA=16 and length=8 fit; SLBA=17 or length=7 do not, even when all other PI fields are correct.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Invalid Key Tag and alignment-related Invalid Field in Command require different investigations; key-tag rejection is not necessarily a PI checksum error.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §5.5; 4.1.5, printed pp. 91-92,105,160, PDF pp. 91-92,105,160

**Related Figures:** 

### Module 35: NVM units and priorities for Streams

**Explanation.** Use two size levels: Stream Write Size and the larger stream granularity. They may be integer multiples of namespace hints, but this is not guaranteed for every namespace.

```text
SWS blocks
  ↓
SGS multiplier
  ↓
Stream granularity
  ↓
Namespace hints
  ↓
Workload
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| SWS | Recommended write size in blocks | Should be a multiple of NPWG |
| SGS × SWS | Length of the stream granularity | Guides stream deallocate alignment/length |
| Priority | Prefer Streams attributes when Streams are used | Otherwise use namespace hints |

**Informative example.** Decoded SWS=8 blocks and SGS=4 give a 32-block stream granularity. An eight-block Write can meet SWS, while deallocating one full granularity unit uses 32 blocks.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Streams hints, FDP placement, and namespace atomicity are different concepts; equal sizes do not prove they identify the same internal media unit.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §5.2.2.3; 5.13, printed pp. 128-129,175, PDF pp. 128-129,175

**Related Figures:** Figure 152

### Module 36: Memory-based resource export template

**Explanation.** The template compatibility interface and underlying device capabilities are separate layers. Check namespace-format compatibility, then configure limits no greater than underlying capabilities; do not advertise capabilities the template does not permit.

```text
Underlying capability
  ↓
Template and TR
  ↓
IDs 0 and 1
  ↓
Set once
  ↓
Reported interface
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| Identity and version | CAP.CSS=1, VS=020300h; NVM VER=010200h | The template fixes Base 2.3/NVM 1.2; the enclosing PDF revision does not upgrade it |
| Controller limits | MDTS, RAB, NCQS, NSQS, MQES, AWUN/AWUPF are bounded by underlying support | NCQS/NSQS are zero-based |
| Namespace compatibility | LBAF0 must match underlying LBADS/MS, with MS=0; DPS/KPIOENS/CWP must be zero | The controller handles Format Index remapping |
| Observable defaults | Error entries and SMART are zero; firmware active slot is 1 | Support lists, Feature defaults, and Identify exceptions have fixed rules |

**Informative example.** Underlying NCQS=7 supports eight queues; configured NCQS=3 permits four queues, not three. A zero namespace NGUID requires a valid NUUID.

**Common mistake / debugging.** Figure 190 says Controller in its caption, but its payload is namespace configuration: decode ENSID, LBAF0, NGUID, and NUUID. Figure 189 teaches the permitted local fields only; other identity fields are not expanded.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §5.4.1-5.4.1.1, printed pp. 152-159, PDF pp. 152-159

**Related Figures:** Figure 183, Figure 184, Figure 185, Figure 186, Figure 187, Figure 188, Figure 189, Figure 190

### Module 37: Exported-state length and consistency

**Explanation.** Read the fixed 64-byte header, then validate variable length and suspension evidence. Configuration state and runtime state differ in purpose and setting constraints; do not share their payload parsers.

```text
Current features
  ↓
CP evidence
  ↓
NVMECSS dwords
  ↓
Bounds
  ↓
Nested VER
```

#### Comparison

| Item | What it answers | Engineering note |
|---|---|---|
| Feature values | Saves arbitration, power, temperature, error recovery, queues, interrupt, atomicity, and AEC | These are current values, not Figure 187 defaults |
| CSATTR.CP | 1 means suspended throughout processing | 0 does not mean there was no suspension at all |
| NVMECSS | Total length = 64 + 4 × NVMECSS bytes | NVMECS is absent when zero |

**Informative example.** With NVMECSS=16, NVMECS occupies 64 bytes and the complete structure 128 bytes. Check multiplication, addition, and receive-buffer bounds before decoding nested VER.

**Common mistake / debugging.** This describes memory-based controller state. A single Feature value cannot establish successful subsystem migration without complete state and suspension evidence.

**Supporting sources:** NVME-NVM-CS-1.3 Rev. 1.3, §5.4.1.2, printed pp. 159-160, PDF pp. 159-160

**Related Figures:** Figure 191

## Source-located specification findings

The mental model above explains causality. This section preserves each source-located conclusion and its normative strength for speaker notes and review.

### 1. Reading map and units

<!-- claim:NVMCS13-FOUNDATION -->

The NVM Command Set supplements Base with logical-block semantics. Logical block data size excludes metadata, whereas logical block size includes it. NVM uses CSI 00h; equal numeric values in commands, Features, logs, and Identify belong to different identifier spaces.

**Explanation.** Place this finding back into the teaching flow: establish object and scope, check capability and state, then convert the field into a software decision. Field presence is not proof of enablement, and a successful completion does not by itself prove that the next lifecycle stage has completed.

> Source: NVME-NVM-CS-1.3, Rev. 1.3, §1.1-1.6; 4.1.3.9; 4.1.4.8; 4.1.5, printed pages 9-12,73-75,79-83, PDF pages 9-12,73-75,79-83

### 2. Namespace capacity and allocation

<!-- claim:NVMCS13-CAPACITY -->

NSZE ≥ NCAP ≥ NUSE: NSZE defines the addressable range, NCAP limits simultaneously allocated blocks, and NUSE counts current allocation. THINP=0 requires NCAP=NSZE. NVMCAP is measured in bytes and is not necessarily NSZE multiplied by data size.

**Explanation.** Place this finding back into the teaching flow: establish object and scope, check capability and state, then convert the field into a software decision. Field presence is not proof of enablement, and a successful completion does not by itself prove that the next lifecycle stage has completed.

> Source: NVME-NVM-CS-1.3, Rev. 1.3, §2.1.1; 4.1.5.1, printed pages 13-14,85-93, PDF pages 13-14,85-93

### 3. Ordering and Compare-and-Write

<!-- claim:NVMCS13-ORDER-FUSED -->

Ordinary commands do not gain LBA dependency ordering merely by sharing an SQ; the host enforces required order. Fused Compare-and-Write compares first and writes only on success; a failed Compare aborts Write with the failed-fused-command status.

**Explanation.** Place this finding back into the teaching flow: establish object and scope, check capability and state, then convert the field into a software decision. Field presence is not proof of enablement, and a successful completion does not by itself prove that the next lifecycle stage has completed.

> Source: NVME-NVM-CS-1.3, Rev. 1.3, §2.1.2-2.1.3, printed pages 14-15, PDF pages 14-15

### 4. Normal, power-fail, and multiple atomicity

<!-- claim:NVMCS13-ATOMIC -->

AWUN/NAWUN and AWUPF/NAWUPF describe normal and failure-condition atomicity. Single Atomicity Mode provides no whole-command guarantee across a boundary; Multiple Atomicity Mode divides the range at boundaries into separately atomic subranges, without promising one combined outcome.

**Explanation.** Place this finding back into the teaching flow: establish object and scope, check capability and state, then convert the field into a software decision. Field presence is not proof of enablement, and a successful completion does not by itself prove that the next lifecycle stage has completed.

> Source: NVME-NVM-CS-1.3, Rev. 1.3, §2.1.4; 4.1.3.4; 5.9, printed pages 15-21,66-67,165, PDF pages 15-21,66-67,165

### 5. Capabilities, opcodes, and status

<!-- claim:NVMCS13-SUPPORT-STATUS -->

An NVM I/O controller must support Read and Write; other listed NVM commands depend on their capability conditions. The low two opcode bits identify transfer direction. Interpret status values with SCT rather than looking up SC alone.

**Explanation.** Place this finding back into the teaching flow: establish object and scope, check capability and state, then convert the field into a software decision. Field presence is not proof of enablement, and a successful completion does not by itself prove that the next lifecycle stage has completed.

> Source: NVME-NVM-CS-1.3, Rev. 1.3, §2.2; 3.1; 3.3, printed pages 22-27, PDF pages 22-27

### 6. Read/Write data and completion

<!-- claim:NVMCS13-READ-WRITE -->

Read/Write specify a contiguous range with SLBA and zero-based NLB. DPTR is a destination buffer for Read and a source buffer for Write. FUA=1 requires nonvolatile-media handling without implying ordering of other commands.

**Explanation.** Place this finding back into the teaching flow: establish object and scope, check capability and state, then convert the field into a software decision. Field presence is not proof of enablement, and a successful completion does not by itself prove that the next lifecycle stage has completed.

> Source: NVME-NVM-CS-1.3, Rev. 1.3, §3.3.4; 3.3.6, printed pages 48-51,53-56, PDF pages 48-51,53-56

### 7. Compare and Verify answer different questions

<!-- claim:NVMCS13-COMPARE-VERIFY -->

Compare compares media data with a host-supplied buffer. Verify checks stored-data integrity without returning data or metadata to the host. Both require PRACT=0; Verify and Read need not report an identical error code for a detected failure.

**Explanation.** Place this finding back into the teaching flow: establish object and scope, check capability and state, then convert the field into a software decision. Field presence is not proof of enablement, and a successful completion does not by itself prove that the next lifecycle stage has completed.

> Source: NVME-NVM-CS-1.3, Rev. 1.3, §3.3.1; 3.3.5, printed pages 27-30,51-53, PDF pages 27-30,51-53

### 8. Copy: source descriptors, contiguous destination, partial failure

<!-- claim:NVMCS13-COPY -->

Copy concatenates one or more source ranges in descriptor order into one contiguous destination range. Formats 0h/1h use one namespace; 2h/3h carry SNSID and require controller support and host enablement. Failure CQE DW0 is the lowest unsuccessful source index; later ranges may already have been copied.

**Explanation.** Place this finding back into the teaching flow: establish object and scope, check capability and state, then convert the field into a software decision. <!-- claim:NVMCS13-COPY-PI -->

Matching Copy formats compare data size, metadata size, DPS, PIFA, significant LBSTM bits, PIF/QPIF, and STS. Corresponding PI formats require PI-only metadata on one side and no metadata on the other; Copy is not a general format converter.

### 10. Dataset Management and three processing limits

<!-- claim:NVMCS13-DSM -->

Dataset Management is advisory: processing attributes does not guarantee deallocation. NR is zero-based; LLB in each 16-byte descriptor is one-based. DMRL, DMRSL, and DMSL constrain range count, individual range length, and total length.

**Explanation.** Place this finding back into the teaching flow: establish object and scope, check capability and state, then convert the field into a software decision. ### 11. Reading deallocated/unwritten blocks

<!-- claim:NVMCS13-DEALLOC -->

When supported and enabled, DULBE makes Copy, Read, Verify, and Compare fail on deallocated/unwritten blocks. Otherwise DRB=001b returns zeros, 010b returns FFh, and 000b allows either; a block must return a deterministic value until its next write.

<!-- claim:NVMCS13-ZERO-UNCORRECTABLE -->

Write Uncorrectable marks a range for unrecovered-read errors. Write Zeroes makes subsequent successful reads return zero data and non-PI metadata. Whole-namespace zeroing with NSZ=1 requires NSZS, DEAC=1, and zero-valued deallocation reads; the host should check CQE.LBACZ.

### 37. Exported-state length and consistency

<!-- claim:NVMCS13-EXPORT-STATE -->

Reference Exported NVM Subsystem State stores current Feature values and controller state. CSATTR.CP=1 means the controller remained suspended throughout Migration Receive processing. NVMECSS gives the variable NVMECS length in dwords; the nested VER is fixed to 1h.

**Explanation.** Place this finding back into the teaching flow: establish object and scope, check capability and state, then convert the field into a software decision. Field presence is not proof of enablement, and a successful completion does not by itself prove that the next lifecycle stage has completed.

> Source: NVME-NVM-CS-1.3, Rev. 1.3, §5.4.1.2, printed pages 159-160, PDF pages 159-160

#### Terms to learn before reading

| Term | Plain-language meaning |
|---|---|

| `AWUPF` | Atomic Write Unit Power Fail, the zero-based atomic size for failure conditions. |
| `ACWU` | Namespace normal/power-fail/compare-and-write or controller compare-and-write atomic size; zero-based. |
| `NAWUN` | Namespace normal/power-fail/compare-and-write or controller compare-and-write atomic size; zero-based. |
| `NAWUPF` | Namespace normal/power-fail/compare-and-write or controller compare-and-write atomic size; zero-based. |
| `NACWU` | Namespace normal/power-fail/compare-and-write or controller compare-and-write atomic size; zero-based. |
| `NABSN` | Normal/power-fail atomic boundary size; interpret zero values and NSABP support using field definitions. |
| `NABSPF` | Normal/power-fail atomic boundary size; interpret zero values and NSABP support using field definitions. |
| `NABO` | Namespace Atomic Boundary Offset; determines the first boundary location. |

#### Read in this order

1. Locate the cited page range and identify raw versus decoded units.
2. Use NSABP to select controller or namespace parameters, then decode zero-based sizes and namespace zero-value inheritance. Raw zero does not universally mean one block.
3. Read size, starting alignment, NSABP, and MAM together. Atomicity and persistence on nonvolatile media are separate checks; FUA/Flush do not establish ordering for other commands.
4. Apply the scenario below and retain the original command, target, and result.

| Stage | Record | Stop condition |
|---|---|---|

| Reading level | Content |
|---|---|

| Boundary | Do not copy the §3.3.2.2 example equating NAWUN=8h with eight blocks: distinguish raw zero-based fields from decoded example sizes. Failed writes may still complete DMA, so buffer transfer completion is not media success. |

**Informative example.** For decoded boundary size 8 blocks and offset zero, a 12-block write starting at LBA 4 splits into [4..7] and [8..15]. Under MAM each part is atomic, not one transaction. Raw AWUN=7h represents eight blocks.

**Common misconception.** Do not copy the §3.3.2.2 example equating NAWUN=8h with eight blocks: distinguish raw zero-based fields from decoded example sizes. Failed writes may still complete DMA, so buffer transfer completion is not media success.

#### Read in this order

1. Locate the cited page range and identify raw versus decoded units.
2. Place boundaries at offset+k×boundary size on the LBA line. A write shorter than the atomic size can still cross a boundary because of its starting position.
3. Read size, starting alignment, NSABP, and MAM together. Atomicity and persistence on nonvolatile media are separate checks; FUA/Flush do not establish ordering for other commands.

**SPEC.** Figure 11, "Protection Information Field Definition": PRACT selects an action and PRCHK selects three checks. With PRACT=1, compare MS with PI size to determine stripping/insertion versus preservation of metadata size. Decode the source-specific fields below.

#### Where this Figure fits

PRACT selects an action and PRCHK selects three checks. With PRACT=1, compare MS with PI size to determine stripping/insertion versus preservation of metadata size.

Field relationships and a worked interpretation, redrawn for this source and revision.

#### Teaching redraw

```text
                                      ↓
```
